subject: FinLytics integration — credentials playbook & implementation plan
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ella Rivera <ella.rivera@finlytics.com>, Marcus Zhou <m.zhou@finlytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: Integration recap + recommended credentials patterns

Hi Ella / Marcus — thanks for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned as you evaluate Redwood for your embeddings + reranker rollout.

Summary of what we covered:
- Target workload: document embeddings + semantic search (200k docs initial), near-realtime reranker on top of candidate list, low single-digit 99th percentile latency target for search.
- Integration surface: backend service (Python/Go) will call Redwood inference; web UI will not hold long-lived keys.
- Compliance: FinLytics requires audit logs, key rotation policy, and separation of duties.

Recommended credentials & auth patterns (priority order):
1) Server-to-server (recommended for backend jobs): Service account with short-lived tokens via OAuth2 client_credentials + JWKS-validated JWTs. Rotate service account keys with customer-managed KMS (if desired).
2) Long-running worker processes: Use service account credentials stored in a secrets manager (e.g., AWS Secrets Manager) and mint short-lived Redwood tokens via a private token-exchange endpoint. Avoid embedding static API keys in the image.
3) Browser/mobile (if any): Do NOT expose long-lived keys. Route through a proxy token exchange or issue ephemeral session tokens scoped to the minimum permissions.

Operational controls we recommend enabling in the initial rollout:
- Per-route API scopes (embeddings-only, generation-only) and separate key sets for inference vs. admin.
- Rotation cadence: rotate root/service credentials quarterly; issue scoped short-lived tokens daily/hours depending on risk profile.
- Audit & trace: enable request-level tracing + token id in logs (we can push a template log format).

Integration notes (SDK + routing):
- Use Redwood SDK for Python (we’ll share a minimal starter) that handles token refresh and KV cache management.
- Route embedding requests to an optimized embedding-only model pool. Reranker calls should go to the low-latency model variant; we can add routing policy in the Console to prefer this pool by region.
- For structured output/tool-calling, include a deterministic response schema and a post-processor that validates shape server-side.

Attachments: an integration checklist and our "credentials playbook" PDF — see attached.

Action items / asks from FinLytics to proceed:
- Confirm preferred auth mode (service accounts w/ client_credentials vs. accepting short-lived API keys).
- Provide security contact for a short questionnaire (SOC2 artifacts / KMS details).
- Confirm a date for a 60-minute technical workshop (we suggested next Tue 4/27 or Thu 4/29).

I can set up a technical deep-dive with Dev from infra and Marissa to cover SDK examples and a sample token-exchange flow.

Thanks,

Tessa Morgan

Hi Ella — quick technical notes and an example flow so you can show your security team. TL;DR: we support both Redwood-managed key rotation and customer-managed KMS; either can meet SOC2 controls but customer-managed KMS gives you stronger separation.

Example: token-exchange flow (high-level)
1) Your backend holds a service-account private key (or uses cloud IAM to generate a signed JWT).
2) Backend calls Redwood token endpoint: POST /v1/token-exchange with client_credentials (JWT) -> returns a short-lived inference token (expires in 1h).
3) Backend uses short-lived token to call embedding/reranker endpoints. Tokens are scoped to routes (embeddings-only).

Curl example (pseudo):

curl -X POST https://api.redwoodinference.com/v1/token-exchange
  -H "Content-Type: application/json"
  -d '{"grant_type":"client_credentials","client_assertion_type":"urn:ietf:params:oauth:client-assertion-type:jwt-bearer","client_assertion":"<signed_jwt>","scope":"embeddings.read"}'

Response: {"access_token":"rwd_tok_abc123","expires_in":3600,"scope":"embeddings.read"}

Key rotation notes:
- If you rotate the service-account key, issue new signed JWTs immediately; existing short-lived tokens remain valid until expiry (max 1h).
- We recommend a staged rotation: create new key, update token minting service, then revoke old key after overlap window (e.g., 24h).
- For emergency revocation, Redwood Console allows immediate revocation of issued tokens for a given service account id.

Scoped credentials: yes, we can issue keys/tokens scoped to specific endpoints (embeddings-only, reranker-only). We can also map multiple credential sets to HubSpot deal metadata for per-project billing.

I'll bring a short demo to the workshop showing the SDK's automatic refresh and how routing rules pin requests to an embeddings pool.
